steps.body: Here's WHY the point never moves. Shade half a chocolate bar. Now cut EVERY piece in half: the cut lines multiply, but the shading stays put. One half became two fourths — **same chocolate, more (smaller) pieces**. That's a fair trade.
Inspector duty: fair trade or robbery?

widget.prompt: Sort each swap: does it keep the amount exactly the same?

items.label: 1 half ↔ 2 fourths
items.feedback: Cut the half in half: two fourths, covering exactly the same chocolate.

items.label: 1 half ↔ 2 sixths
items.feedback: Two sixths only make a THIRD — sixths are smaller than fourths. Whoever took this trade lost chocolate.

items.label: 1 third ↔ 2 sixths
items.feedback: Cut the third in half: two sixths, same amount to the crumb.

items.label: 1 fourth ↔ 2 eighths
items.feedback: One fourth splits into exactly two eighths — a clean, even trade.

widget.missFeedback: A fair trade cuts the SAME piece into equal mini-pieces — the swap must rebuild exactly the original.
widget.successFeedback: Halves→fourths, thirds→sixths, fourths→eighths all trade clean; 2 sixths for a half is a robbery (that's only a third).

predict.prompt: Cutting every piece of a bar in half — does the shaded AMOUNT change?
predict.reveal: The cuts multiply the count and shrink the size in perfect balance — 2/4 covers exactly the ground 1/2 did. That balance IS equivalence.

explanationVariants: The knife added lines, not chocolate — the shaded half now reads 2/4, but its edges never moved.
Twice the pieces, each half the size: twice × half = the same amount.

widget.prompt: A bar has 1/2 shaded. You cut every piece in half. The shaded part now reads…

options.label: 2/4 — the same amount, renamed
options.feedback: New lines, same shading: the half is now called two fourths.

options.label: 1/4 — cutting halved it
options.feedback: The PIECES got halved, not the shading. The shaded region kept both of its new fourth-pieces: 2/4.

options.label: 2/2 — the whole bar
options.feedback: 2/2 would mean ALL pieces shaded. Only the original half is — which is 2 of the 4 new pieces.
Eighths would need another round of cutting — and even then, the shaded amount would read 4/8, not 1/8.

steps.body: The trade rule, in words: cut every piece into the same number of mini-pieces, and BOTH counts grow together — total pieces and taken pieces alike. The amount stands still. That's why **1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8**: fair trades, all the way down.

explanationVariants: Cut each half into 3 minis: the whole becomes 6 pieces, and your half becomes 3 of them — 3/6.
Check it on the line: 3 of 6 jumps is halfway, exactly 1/2's spot.

widget.prompt: You hold 1/2 of a bar and trade it into SIXTHS (each half gets cut into 3 minis). How many sixths do you hold?

commonErrors.feedback: 6 sixths is the WHOLE bar. You only held half of it — half of the 6 pieces is 3.
2 copied the bottom of 1/2 — but the trade is into sixths now. Your half-bar cuts into 3 of the 6 minis.

widget.fallbackFeedback: The whole becomes 6 minis; your half is half of them.

steps.body: Why can't the amount move? Step through it.

panels.title: Knives add lines, not chocolate
panels.body: When you cut every piece in half, you draw new lines INSIDE the bar. The shaded region's outer edges never move a hair.

panels.title: Twice the pieces, half the size
panels.body: Your shaded part now holds twice as many pieces — but each is half as big. Twice as many × half as big = exactly what you had.

panels.title: Renaming, never resizing
panels.body: That's all equal fractions are: the same amount with a new name. 1/2, 2/4, 4/8 — one region, three labels.

widget.continueFeedback: Keep going — the trade's secret is in the next panel.
widget.successFeedback: Cutting finer renames the amount without resizing it — the whole story of equivalent fractions.

explanationVariants: Cut each third in half: the 3 pieces become 6, and your 2 pieces become 4 — 4/6, same amount.
Both counts must grow by the SAME cutting: 2→4 taken and 3→6 total is one clean halving of every piece.

widget.prompt: Which is a FAIR trade for 2/3?

options.feedback: Every third cut in half: 2 taken become 4, 3 total become 6. The amount never flinched.
Adding 1 to top and bottom isn't a trade — no cutting does that. It quietly changes the amount (3/4 is more than 2/3).
The total was traded (3→6) but your taken pieces weren't (still 2) — you'd lose half your chocolate. Both counts must grow together.
4/3 is MORE than a whole bar — no fair trade turns two-thirds into that. Trades rename amounts, never grow them.

hints: Trade fourths for eighths: cut each fourth in half.
You hold 3 fourths — trade them one by one.
explanationVariants: Each of your 3 fourths splits into 2 eighths: 3 × 2 = 6 eighths — and 6/8 stands on 3/4's exact spot.
The whole bar becomes 8 pieces; your share keeps its edges and now counts 6 of them.

widget.prompt: You hold 3/4 of a bar and trade it into EIGHTHS. How many eighths do you hold?

commonErrors.feedback: 8 eighths is the whole bar — you hold three-quarters of it. Each of your 3 fourths trades for 2 eighths.
7 added the 3 and the 4 — but adding tops to bottoms isn't a trade. Cut each of your 3 fourths in half: 3 × 2.

widget.fallbackFeedback: One fourth = two eighths. Trade your three fourths piece by piece.

takeaways: Cutting finer renames an amount — it never resizes it.
Fair trade = every piece cut the same way, so both counts grow together.
Test any trade on the bar or the line, never by digit patterns.
steps.teaser: one more disguise to unmask: whole numbers hiding inside fractions.

concept.body: Quick rewind. Think money: **one half-dollar trades for 2 quarters** — nobody gets richer or poorer. Fair fraction trades work the same: swap a piece for the minis that exactly rebuild it, and the amount can't change.

explanationVariants: One half-piece splits into exactly two fourth-pieces — a clean trade, same amount.
Like the half-dollar for two quarters: 1/2 = 2/4.

widget.prompt: One HALF of a bar trades fairly for how many FOURTH-pieces?

options.feedback: Cut the half in half: two fourths, same chocolate.
Four fourths would be the WHOLE bar — that trade steals the other half. Your half rebuilds from 2 fourths.
One fourth is only half of your half — you'd lose chocolate. It takes 2 fourths to rebuild a half.
